title: Telemetry-aware reconnect policy and fragment fingerprint for resumable streams
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Current SSE/HTTP streaming reconnects rely on either full-line JSON checkpoints or opaque resume tokens that lack fine-grained fragment provenance. This causes replays to be inefficient, makes function_call/structured-output boundaries brittle, and results in user-visible duplicate function calls in a minority of reconnect cases.

Objective: Implement a telemetry-aware reconnect policy combined with a lightweight fragment fingerprinting scheme so clients and servers can: (1) negotiate minimal resume points, (2) detect and dedupe fragments deterministically, and (3) preserve tool/function_call atomicity across reconnects while remaining compatible with legacy JSONL/SSE consumers.

Scope and constraints:
- Streaming layer must remain compatible with legacy clients that only expect newline-delimited JSON events.
- No per-token signing or heavy crypto in the hot path; fingerprints should be cheap (e.g., 32-bit/64-bit truncated XXHash or Murmur variant).
- Telemetry (latency percentiles, error counters, retransmit counts) must feed automatic backoff tuning but not leak PII.
- Implementation must support both hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments (configurable behavior behind feature flags).

Design summary:
1) Fragment fingerprint: server emits a short ASCII-safe fingerprint header in an SSE comment event and a companion JSON field for structured consumers. Format: "fingerprint":"f:<hex>". Fingerprint covers the fragment payload (post-json-serialization) plus a stream-seq and truncated checksum. Clients use fingerprint equality to dedupe.
2) Resume negotiation: On reconnect, clients send last-seen fingerprint(s) and a small resume window hint (e.g., 3 fragments). Server attempts to locate an exact fingerprint match in recent fragment cache and, if found, responds with a resume cursor that references an internal stable snapshot id + offset. If not found, server falls back to last full checkpoint (JSONL boundary) or signals full reset.
3) Telemetry-aware policy: Client includes measured downstream latency histogram and reconnect cause tags (client-probed, network-error, auth-refresh) in the reconnect handshake. Server adjusts recommended backoff/jitter and may proactively offer reduced-batch variants or alternate model variants to keep latency SLO.
4) Atomic function_call boundaries: Fragments that contain function_call entries include an explicit atomicity flag and a compact function_call_id that is included in the fingerprint calculation. Reassembly logic ensures that partial deliveries that cross reconnects are either deduped or retried via server-confirmed idempotency metadata.
5) Legacy compatibility: If a client does not support fingerprint fields or resume handshake, server continues to use existing resume-token behavior. New behavior is opt-in via handshake header 'X-RI-Resume-V2: 1'.

Trade-offs considered:
- Using a short fingerprint reduces bandwidth and CPU but increases collision risk; chosen truncation gives collision probability <1e-12 for typical fragment rates.
- Storing recent fragments for resume increases memory and cache complexity on the server; mitigated with bounded LRU cache and configurable retention window per deployment tier.
- Adding telemetry fields to handshake increases metadata surface; we separate telemetry from customer content and roll out with data retention rules.

Deliverables:
- Runtime patch: fingerprint generation, fragment cache, resume lookup, and handshake parsing.
- Client SDK updates: JS/Go clients accept fingerprint comments, send resume hints, and implement dedupe.
- Console: per-stream resume metrics, dedupe rate, and recommended backoff policy UI.
- E2E tests and a small chaos experiment to validate reconnect behavior under packet loss.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Fragment+Fingerprint+and+Resume+V2
- PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2489
- PR (js-sdk): https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/394
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/resume-metrics

Success criteria:
- 95% reduction in duplicate function_call deliveries observed in reconciliation tests.
- Median reconnect resume latency under 200ms for warm fragment cache cases.
- No regression on SSE throughput benchmarks (>98% of baseline).
comments: 2026-02-10 - Ava Chen: Created ticket after postmortem for incident INC-2026-01 where duplicated tool invocations were observed during a region flip. Initial design drafted in Confluence.
2026-02-15 - Diego Ramirez: Spike completed for fingerprint generation; 64-bit truncated xxhash chosen for speed. Microbenchmarks attached to PR #2489 show <0.5% CPU overhead at 1k rps per worker.
2026-02-18 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Asked for explicit opt-in in Dedicated/Private until we finalize privacy docs. Added retention settings to design.
2026-02-22 - Security (Rashid Khan): Reviewed telemetry fields. OK if we strip any identifiers and enforce retention TTLs. Added to security checklist.
2026-02-25 - Diego Ramirez: Implemented server-side LRU fragment cache with configurable max entries. Pushed runtime patch to branch feat/resume-v2. See PR #2489.
2026-02-26 - Review (Laura Silva, infra): Concerned about cache warmup during autoscale events; recommend persisting minimal metadata to redis during scale-up. Added follow-up sub-issue ENG-527489.
2026-03-01 - Diego Ramirez: Integration tests added for function_call boundary dedupe; failing case discovered with HTTP/2 multiplexing where fragment order can be non-deterministic. Investigating.
2026-03-01 - QA (Samir Patel): Assigned to run chaos experiment (packet loss and mid-stream auth-refresh). Planned start 2026-03-05.
2026-03-01 - Next steps: Stabilize HTTP/2 ordering handling, implement optional Redis-backed fragment index for warmup, and prepare SDK release notes for opt-in header.
notes: Keep the resume window conservative by default (3 fragments). Ops can increase for Dedicated customers. Rollout gated by feature flag 'resume_v2' and config 'fragment_cache_max'.
